content.user_title: Manage Git Pull Requests and Branch Workflows
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent branch names, PR descriptions, and review checklists. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical Git workflow decisions.
actual_capabilities: Creates structured pull request descriptions with summaries, test plans, and checklists.
Recommends branch naming conventions using type, issue number, and short description fields.
Explains when to use squash, merge, or rebase strategies.
Helps document breaking changes with migration notes.
Provides quick templates for feature, bug fix, and refactor pull requests.
limitations: It does not run Git commands or inspect repository state by itself.
It cannot verify that tests passed unless the user provides results.
It does not enforce repository branch protection settings.
It depends on team conventions supplied by the user.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Create a clear PR body with summary, motivation, changes, tests, screenshots, and breaking change notes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Branches
use_cases.description: Define branch naming rules that match issue tracking and conventional change types.

use_cases.title: Improve Review Quality
use_cases.description: Add practical checklists that help reviewers confirm tests, documentation, warnings, and issue links.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic PR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request description for this change. Include a summary, motivation, changes, test plan, checklist, and breaking changes section.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user preparing a first complete pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Name a Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest a branch name for this work using type, issue number, and a short description. Explain why the type fits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer starting work from an issue or ticket.

prompt_templates.title: Review PR Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request description for clarity, missing test details, breaking change notes, screenshots, and issue links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Reviewer checking whether a PR is ready for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Merge Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a merge strategy for this branch. Consider commit history, audit needs, review size, and whether a linear history matters.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user choosing between squash, merge, and rebase.

output_examples.input: A developer added OAuth login and needs a pull request description.
output_examples.output: A complete PR draft with a feature summary, user motivation, added authentication details, test checklist, screenshot prompt, and breaking change section.

output_examples.input: A team wants branch names linked to ticket numbers.
output_examples.output: A branch naming recommendation such as feature, fix, refactor, docs, test, or chore, with guidance for issue number and short description use.

output_examples.input: A maintainer is unsure whether to squash or merge a feature branch.
output_examples.output: A merge strategy recommendation based on history clarity, audit trail needs, branch size, and team review expectations.

best_practices: Provide the ticket number, change summary, and test results before asking for PR text.
Use the same branch type labels across repositories and documentation.
Document breaking changes with clear migration steps.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague PR summaries that only repeat the title.
Do not claim tests passed without providing actual results.
Do not choose a merge strategy without considering team history rules.

faq.question: Can this skill create pull request templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides full PR body sections and quick templates for feature, bug fix, and refactor work.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and templates, but it does not execute Git commands by itself.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with branch naming?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends names using a change type, issue number, and short description.

faq.question: Can it choose a merge strategy?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains squash, merge, and rebase options based on team needs.

faq.question: Is it suitable for code review process changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps define checklists for tests, documentation, warnings, screenshots, and linked issues.
